title: A complete set of polymerases that synthesize in the 3′-to-5′ direction

concept.text: Millennium Problems for Biology 11, 5′ polymerases. Target: a complete set of polymerases acting in the 3′ to 5′ direction (DNA polymerase, RNA polymerase, reverse transcriptase and RNA-dependent RNA polymerase) with processivity and error rates matching or exceeding Taq, T7 RNA polymerase, M-MLV reverse transcriptase and Phi 6 RdRP. Sources given: https://millenniumproblems.bio/.

change_log.change: Added by hand to BCH on 2026-11-15.
change_log.reason: One of the twelve Millennium Problems for Biology (Sam Rodriques and Michaela Hinks, FutureHouse and Edison Scientific, 2026), each with a stated concrete target; added at the owner's request, November 14, 2026.

page.title: A complete set of 3′–5′ polymerases
page.definition: Enzymes synthesize nucleic acids by adding nucleotides at a strand’s 5′ end, so the product grows 3′→5′. The set covers four template→product combinations: DNA→DNA, DNA→RNA, RNA→DNA and RNA→RNA.

goal.need: The challenge covers four template/product combinations. A study published in October 2024 demonstrated template-directed addition of up to eight RNA nucleotides at a strand’s 5′ end. Its stated application is adding sequences or labels to RNA after transcription without ligation, the joining of pre-existing strands. The complete set extends the target beyond this RNA-dependent RNA activity.

statements.quote: Produce a full set of polymerases that act in the 5′ direction.
Each problem is intended to be very difficult to solve, but easy to validate in a simple laboratory environment.
statements.context: The announcement published on 23 September 2026 introduces twelve challenges, including 5′ polymerases.

completion.title: Four 3′–5′ polymerase classes match their comparators in processivity and copying error frequency.
completion.criterion: Demonstrate 3′–5′ DNA→DNA, DNA→RNA, RNA→DNA and RNA→RNA synthesis. For each class, average nucleotides added per enzyme-binding event must be at least its comparator’s, and errors per copied nucleotide must be no greater, using comparable measurements. The respective comparators are Taq DNA polymerase, T7 RNA polymerase, M-MLV reverse transcriptase and Phi 6 RNA-dependent RNA polymerase. These inequalities are the Atlas operational interpretation; the challenge specifies neither assays nor numerical acceptance bounds.
completion.set_by: Atlas, operationalizing FutureHouse and Edison Scientific’s Millennium Problems for Biology, problem 11.
completion.basis: Problem 11 supplies comparators and the phrase “similar to or superior”, but no assay-defined acceptance test. Searches for reverse-polymerase standards, prize rules, roadmaps and benchmark protocols found none. This fallback requires parity rather than assigning an unsupported tolerance to “similar”. Processivity is measured per binding event, following published biochemical practice.

milestones.title: An enzyme adds a template-directed nucleotide to a nucleic acid’s 5′ end.
milestones.criterion: For the case’s template/product combination, demonstrate enzyme-catalysed addition of at least one complementary nucleotide at a primer’s 5′ end through a standard phosphodiester bond. The paper published on 26 May 2006 demonstrated templated RNA extension and deoxyguanosine incorporation into RNA. The latter establishes deoxynucleotide acceptance, without demonstrating an all-DNA product. Replicate counts were not stated for these assays. The DNA-template cases remain unverified in the sources found.
milestones.set_by: Atlas; searches of Thg1 studies and reverse-polymerase roadmaps found no external staged criterion. This chemical demonstration is generalized across cases.

milestones.title: An enzyme adds at least two templated nucleotides to a primer’s 5′ end using a separate template.
milestones.criterion: Demonstrate successive template-directed additions to the same primer using a separate template oligonucleotide. Two additions are the minimal Atlas interpretation of repeated polymerization. In October 2024, DdiTLP4, a Thg1-like protein, produced the expected eight-nucleotide extension of a 26-nucleotide RNA primer. The study’s kinetic measurements used three independent experiments. This supports the RNA-templated RNA case; the study did not test the other three template/product combinations.
milestones.set_by: Atlas; no external intermediate acceptance threshold was found. The separate-primer demonstration published by Jayasinghe and colleagues concerned RNA-templated RNA synthesis.

milestones.title: A 3′–5′ polymerase equals or exceeds its class comparator’s processivity.
milestones.criterion: For one case, demonstrate average extension per enzyme-binding event at least equal to the comparator specified in the completion criterion, using corresponding substrates and comparable measurements. The published processivity assay distinguishes single binding events from repeated binding and extension. The 2024 reverse-polymerase experiments used enzyme excess and did not establish comparator-level processivity.
milestones.set_by: Atlas; searches found no external individual-class processivity qualification protocol. This milestone separates one component of problem 11’s target.

milestones.title: A 3′–5′ polymerase reaches comparator processivity with no higher copying error frequency.
milestones.criterion: For one case, retain the processivity result and demonstrate errors per copied nucleotide no greater than its comparator’s. A June 2021 study tested yeast Thg1 with four template bases and four incoming nucleotides, using at least three independent assays per combination. Incorrect/correct incorporation-efficiency ratios ranged from 10⁻¹ to 10⁻⁶; these kinetic ratios do not establish comparator-level copying accuracy. This milestone qualifies an individual case; completion requires the full set.
milestones.set_by: Atlas; searches found no external individual-class qualification protocol. This applies problem 11’s two performance requirements to each case separately.

not_found: Searches found no numerical definition of “similar”, prescribed assay, sequence panel or acceptance statistics for problem 11.
Searches found no externally adopted staged roadmap or qualification protocol for the complete reverse-polymerase set.
Searches found no experimental demonstration of DNA-templated 3′–5′ DNA or RNA synthesis.
Searches found no complete set, or individual reverse-polymerase class, tested against both of its specified comparator characteristics.
The PMC page for the 2021 fidelity paper presented a browser check; the journal’s full-text PDF was opened.

results.finding: AcaTLP2 and DdiTLP4 extended RNA using an RNA template by up to 8 bases; endpoint assay replicate count not stated.
results.detail: The study describes template-dependent incorporation at the RNA substrate’s 5′ end and standard phosphodiester-bond chemistry. Kinetic assays were performed in triplicate.
results.quote: Using optimized assay conditions, we demonstrated a remarkable capacity of certain TLPs to accommodate short RNA substrate-template duplexes of varying lengths with significantly high affinity, resulting in the ability to incorporate a desired nucleotide sequence of up to eight bases to 5′-ends of the model RNA substrates in a template-dependent manner.

results.finding: DdiTLP4 extended an RNA primer by 8 nucleotides; kinetic measurements used 3 independent experiments.
results.detail: A separate RNA oligonucleotide supplied the template. Kinetic assays tracked shorter products as they appeared and were converted into longer products.
results.quote: Again, DdiTLP4 extended each substrate with a major product that corresponds to the expected 8-nt addition, although the overall efficiency of extension appeared to improve with shorter duplexes.

results.finding: Yeast Thg1 incorporated deoxyguanosine into RNA; at least 1 deoxynucleotide was added. Replicate count not stated.
results.detail: The RNA substrate supported template-directed reverse polymerization, and Thg1 accepted dGTP. The study did not demonstrate synthesis of an all-DNA product from an RNA template.
results.quote: Thus, dGTP is incorporated and not contaminating GTP.

results.finding: Yeast Thg1, ≥3 assays per RNA/NTP combination: base-substitution kinetic ratios ranged from 10⁻¹ to 10⁻⁶.
results.detail: Single-turnover incorporation efficiencies bear on fidelity, but do not establish errors per copied nucleotide or retain a comparator-level processivity result.
